description: Use this when someone asks how many sheets of drywall or plasterboard, screws, tape or joint compound they need. Calculates the drywall for a room: the wall area 2 × (length + width) × height, or a given area, less the doors and windows (36 × 80 in and 36 × 60 in each unless given), plus the ceiling (length × width) when asked; the area with waste (10 % unless given; Georgia-Pacific advises 10 to 15 %); and the sheets, rounded up. Sheets: 4x8, 4x10 and 4x12 ft, and metric boards 600, 1200 and 1250 mm wide; sheetWidth and sheetLength together replace them. With 2 layers, the board area and the screws double. It also returns, for the area to cover and without waste, the joint compound in compoundUnit and the joint tape in millimeters for the outer layer, and the screws for all layers, each the area times its rate per square meter of board. Rates when not given (USG): 9.4 gal of ready-mixed compound per 1,000 sq ft (0.383 l/m²), 370 ft of tape per 1,000 sq ft (1.214 m/m²), and screws 1,000 per 1,000 sq ft on framing 16 in on center (10.76/m²), 850 on framing 24 in on center (9.15/m²), Gypsum Construction Handbook. Other makers give their own rates per square meter, such as about 0.35 to 0.45 kg of powder compound and 1.4 to 1.6 m of tape in Europe and Brazil. Areas are in square meters (1 sq ft = 0.09290304 m²; 1 US gallon = 3.785411784 l).

ceiling.description: True to board the ceiling too; needs length and width.

ceilingScrewRate.description: Screws per square meter of board on the ceiling, such as 14 on battens 500 mm apart (Chausson); screwRate when left out.

ceilingTapeRate.description: Joint tape in millimeters per square meter of board on the ceiling, such as 1600 (Chausson); tapeRate when left out.

compoundRate.description: Joint compound per square meter of board in compoundUnit, such as 0.35 kg of powder; USG's 0.383 l of ready-mixed compound when left out, which needs compoundUnit l.

compoundUnit.description: l: liters of ready-mixed compound; kg: kilograms of powder or of ready-mixed compound; l when left out.

doorHeight.description: Height of one door; 2032 (80 in) when left out, in millimeters.

doorWidth.description: Width of one door; 914.4 (36 in) when left out, in millimeters.

doors.description: Number of doors to leave out; none when left out.

framing.description: Spacing of the studs and joists on center, in millimeters: 400 (16 in) or 600 (24 in), which picks USG's screws when screwRate is left out; 400 when left out.

height.description: Wall height, floor to ceiling, in millimeters.

innerScrewRate.description: Screws per square meter of the inner of two layers, such as 3 under an outer layer of 8 at 600 mm (Fassa Gypsotech); the outer layer's rate when left out.

layers.description: Layers of board on each surface, 1 or 2; 1 when left out.

screwRate.description: Screws per square meter of board on the walls, as the board maker gives them, such as 12 on battens 600 mm apart (Chausson); USG's by framing when left out.

sheet.description: 4x8, 4x10 and 4x12 are US sheets in feet; the others are metric boards, width x length in millimeters.

sheetLength.description: Board length of a size of its own, which replaces the sheet; give sheetWidth with it, in millimeters.

sheetWidth.description: Board width of a size of its own, which replaces the sheet; give sheetLength with it, in millimeters.

tapeRate.description: Joint tape in millimeters per square meter of board on the walls, such as 1500; USG's 1214 when left out; 0 for boards whose edges need no tape.

walls.description: Area to board in square meters, used instead of length, width and height.

waste.description: Percent added for cutting and piecing; 10 when left out.

windowHeight.description: Height of one window; 1524 (60 in) when left out, in millimeters.

windowWidth.description: Width of one window; 914.4 (36 in) when left out, in millimeters.

windows.description: Number of windows to leave out; none when left out.
